description: We are scientists who will reveal the Hi
summary: Vesta turns NASA FIRMS hotspot detections from MODIS and VIIRS into one consistent monthly calendar. Satellite sensors count different numbers of fires for the same reality. When VIIRS began in 2012, raw counts jumped, which looks like a trend but is a sensor change. Vesta translates older MODIS counts to what S-NPP VIIRS would have counted, so any month can be compared with the same month in other years. Emergency managers can see whether a month is unusual for their area, and download the numbers as CSV.
details:
Live app link: https://app-nine-lyart-38.vercel.app

What it does: a calendar of hotspots by year and month, a check of whether the latest full month is unusual compared with earlier years, and a CSV download. The live app covers Punjab, the Delhi box, and the Mumbai box, plus any custom box inside them.

How it works: we read the NASA FIRMS archive and near-real-time files for MODIS (Terra and Aqua) and VIIRS (S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21), about 18 million detections after cleaning. We aggregate by 5-degree tile and month. We calibrate Aqua, Terra and NOAA-20 against S-NPP per tile and month. The calibration model is chosen by leave-one-year-out cross-validation, with one year held out for testing. Estimated values are flagged. Each release is versioned and checksummed.

Results (release 2026.11.3, national totals): the naive raw sum shows a jump of +632% across 2012 (95% range +496% to +786%). The harmonized series shows -4.9% (95% range -23.2% to +17.5%), a range that includes zero, so no significant jump remains.

Cross-validation (region SMAPE, lower is better): AQUA 25.9, TERRA 35.7, NOAA-20 7.0, NOAA-21 9.2. Interval coverage at 95%: 89.4%, 88.9%, 94.2%, 94.6%.

Why it matters: MODIS is nearing the end of its operational life. NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 are its successors. A consistent record is needed for early warning.

Limits: hotspots are thermal detections, not fires and not burned area. Before 2012 we cannot check values against ground truth, so we report cross-validation only. Several 2026 months show satellite coverage gaps in the release, so their values are not compared. The Mumbai box has small counts, so its percentiles are not stable. October 2026 is held pending review. Static industrial sources are flagged but not matched to named plants. FRP and FIRE_DAYS are not harmonized in this release. Only three areas are live.

Team Hi: Sanay (group leader; web app, contracts, release and decisions), Vishwa (science and calibration; analytics library), Adithya (API, QA and deployment), Sharli (data pipeline, docs and pitch).

Tools: Python (pandas, DuckDB, pandera, FastAPI, pytest, ruff); TypeScript and Next.js; static HTML and JavaScript; GitHub Copilot and Claude for development.
